headline: MIT CSAIL: GPT-6 Astra reads and edits neural network weights directly
quote: fixes this by natively editing 0.016% of the weights. With the same sampling settings, this weight correction raises MATH-500 from 7.9% to 48.1%
claim: A 2 Nov 2026 MIT CSAIL write-up says GPT-6 Astra, by editing 0.016% of Qwen3.5-0.8B's weights without gradients, raised MATH-500 from 7.9% to 48.1%. Simon Willison reports critics say it conflates two questions and that a Qwen 3.8 27B model on a laptop can do the no-tools weight-reading task.
why_it_matters: A reproducible interpretability experiment: the prompts are public, and you can try the weight-reading task on a local model with LM Studio.
title: Sparks of Weight-Space Programming: LLMs can natively read & write neural network weights

headline: Claude Code adds MCP tasks that run in the background in terminal
quote: when an MCP server runs a tool call as a task, Claude Code moves it to the background
claim: The 6 Nov 2026 Claude Code changelog entry adds terminal support for MCP tasks, which move to the background and report back when finished; CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_MCP_TASK_BACKGROUND makes Claude wait instead.
why_it_matters: Long-running MCP tools no longer block your Claude Code session, so you can keep working while a slow job finishes.
title: Claude Code changelog - Claude Code Docs

headline: Cursor adds realtime voice chat with agents, powered by Grok Voice
quote: You can now talk with your agents in a realtime voice call.
claim: Cursor's 6 Nov 2026 changelog says voice chat works in the Agents Window, IDE, web and Cursor for iOS, runs on Grok Voice, and uses zero data retention with Privacy Mode on.
why_it_matters: You can direct and check on coding agents by voice, handy when away from the keyboard; start it with the waveform button.
title: What's New in Cursor — Latest Updates & Release Notes

headline: US Democrats plan AI bills on independent model evaluation and liability
quote: plans to push legislation requiring independent experts to evaluate leading AI models against safety standards
claim: Rep. Lori Trahan plans legislation requiring independent experts to evaluate leading AI models against safety standards, and a bill clarifying that companies can be held responsible when AI systems act in harmful ways, according to her deputy chief of staff, as Democrats prepare to take control of Congress.
why_it_matters: Signals the direction of US AI rules in 2027; third-party evaluation work is a growing field to learn.
title: Democrats Planning Flood of AI Bills When They Take Control of Congress
